clue.text: French are to get better of English in breakout

parts.note: es is the French for '(you) are', as in tu es
to cap is to outdo or better someone

explanation.surface: A French prisoner outwitting an English guard during a jailbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout from prison is a getaway, the same noun sense as a flight to freedom.

clue.text: Not good to accept line showing too much pizazz?

indicators.note: to accept means the first word takes the next letter inside itself

parts.note: sick means unwell, not in good health

explanation.surface: Someone criticises an over-flashy performance as distastefully showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slick describes something glib and over-polished, with flashiness laid on too thick.

clue.text: A new driver ruined more of a car

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a new driver's car

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of these words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A learner driver has crashed and wrecked more of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alfa Romeo is an Italian make of motor vehicle, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Drawing out end of debate's allowed in Government

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word debate, whose 's is a link

parts.note: licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Extracting the conclusion of a parliamentary debate is permitted within government.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw a response out of someone, so the participle is a synonym of drawing out.

clue.text: Unhappy season in America leading to collapse

parts.note: down means low in spirits, unhappy
autumn is called fall in American English

explanation.surface: A miserable American autumn precedes some breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a ruin or collapse, as of a regime or a person's fortunes.

clue.text: Regularly doing work on historic site?

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the following word, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An archaeologist regularly at work on an ancient site.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaeological excavation is called a dig, the work done at a historic site.

clue.text: Married, embracing endless passion? That's odd

indicators.note: embracing means the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: wed means married

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion

explanation.surface: A wedded couple without passion — a strange state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and odd are synonyms, both meaning strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Foot? Shorter measure will do for small bird

parts.note: an inch is a smaller unit of length than a foot

explanation.surface: Someone decides a shorter unit than a foot will suffice.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch is a type of small seed-eating songbird, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Red column destroyed in spread of yellow?

indicators.note: destroyed says these letters are broken up and rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A red pillar wrecked and smeared across a yellow surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This preserve is a yellow sweet paste made from citrus, butter and eggs, spread on toast.

clue.text: Trivial romantic adventure devout female has put behind her?

indicators.note: put behind means the fling comes after the devout woman's letters

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, devout
a fling is a brief romantic affair

explanation.surface: A pious woman dismisses a past affair as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffling means trifling or worthless, a colloquial synonym of trivial.

clue.text: Pub, one generated by the writer for fictional purposes

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a means one
the writer means the setter, who calls himself me

explanation.surface: A pub invented by an author for a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held only nominally, rather than in reality, is a fiction maintained for appearances.

clue.text: Runner runs miles — I peel off, mildly conflicted?

parts.note: a ski is a runner, like that of a sledge
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to shed is to peel off a skin or layer

explanation.surface: A jogger covering miles and stripping off, torn about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a minor fight, so to have skirmished is to have been in a light clash.

clue.text: Under pressure, hastened to get round a classic car

indicators.note: getting round means the hastening word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: hied is an old word for hastened
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a classic car marque

explanation.surface: A stressed driver races to make a circuit in a vintage car.
explanation.definitionFit: Harried means harassed or pestered, under stress from repeated demands.

clue.text: Worker cheated, acquiring note

indicators.note: acquiring means the cheating word takes in the next letter

parts.note: had means cheated, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: A labourer who was swindled gets a banknote back.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm or factory labourer is called a hand, as in 'all hands on deck'.

clue.text: More settled, rising star takes motor-racing on board

indicators.note: takes means the star's letters include something
on board means carried inside the star word

parts.note: a comer is someone on the way up, a rising star
F1 is Formula One motor-racing, written FI

explanation.surface: A promising young star signs up for motor-racing.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is written FI, the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfier means cosier, more comfortably settled in.

clue.text: Mystic British island cracking mould

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into the mould word

parts.note: a cast is a mould
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A British islander breaks out of the mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabbalist studies the Kabbalah, Jewish esoteric mysticism, so is a mystic.

clue.text: Very threatening look limits a display of bravery

indicators.note: limits means the surrounding letters enclose the short word

parts.note: to lour is to scowl, a threatening look

explanation.surface: A very menacing glare contains a hint of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Valour is courage shown in the face of danger.

clue.text: Rule on vet upset reservist?

indicators.note: upset says these letters are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A rule on veterinary surgeons causes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Territorial Army reservists are part-time soldiers who offer their service unpaid, so an example.

clue.text: Story about millions coming to land gets attention

indicators.note: coming to means the next word follows on
about means the story word goes around the next letter

parts.note: a lie is a story, a tall tale
to light is to land or alight

explanation.surface: A tale of millions arriving ashore grabs the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight means being the focus of public notice.

clue.text: One revisiting school, perhaps, getting ache in quad?

parts.note: an old boy, OB, might return to his school
to long is to ache with desire

explanation.surface: A former pupil feels nostalgia in the school quadrangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quad' looks like the school quadrangle; it is short for quadrilateral.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided figure, a quadrilateral, here shortened to quad.

clue.text: Unwell, was annoyed to miss start of festival getting lit up

parts.note: ill means unwell

indicators.note: to miss means the next letter is left out

parts.note: fumed means was angry

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of festival

explanation.surface: Someone sick was irritated to miss the opening of a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss start of festival' removes F from FUMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumed is a poetic form of illuminated, meaning lit up.

clue.text: Product of acid reaction settled around lake

indicators.note: around means the seated word goes round the next letter

parts.note: sat means settled, as on a seat

explanation.surface: A chemistry deposit has settled around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an acid and a base react to give this compound and water.

clue.text: Speeds I encountered going uphill round top of Pyrenees

indicators.note: round means the reversed letters go around the next one
in a down clue going uphill means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of Pyrenees

explanation.surface: A cyclist recounts racing uphill in the Pyrenees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going uphill' turns IMET into TEMI, which wraps around P.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, tempi is the plural of tempo, the speeds at which pieces are played.

clue.text: Translation of lingo's held to be historic language

indicators.note: translation renders the letters into another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A translation of some jargon is thought to be an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Saxon, spoken before about 1150, is the earliest form of English.

clue.text: Razor specialist set up company: arrived for a trim

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, backwards
a trim cuts off the end letter of the word

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: A barber founds a firm and comes in for a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Ockham devised the principle called Occam's razor, so he is its specialist.

clue.text: Pip found in apple, not spinach, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
found in says the letters are sitting inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A seed turns up in an apple rather than spinach.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Pip found' as the definition, but 'found in' is the indicator for the concealed letters, leaving 'Pip' alone as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pip or seed is also called a stone, as in a plum or cherry.

clue.text: Money collected by fellow I left in charge of cinema

indicators.note: collected by means the money letter is picked up by the preceding letters

parts.note: M is short for money, as in M3

explanation.surface: A fellow pockets cash, leaving someone in charge of the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Filmic is an adjective meaning relating to films and movie-making.

clue.text: Fish ultimately outstanding in nutriment, making you happier

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the nourishment word

parts.note: food is nutriment
an eel is a fish

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word outstanding

explanation.surface: Fish is an outstanding cheer-up food.
explanation.definitionFit: A feel-good film or factor is one that lifts the mood, raising spirits.

clue.text: Target of PETA's endless anger?

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: fury is great anger

explanation.surface: Animal-rights group PETA rages without end at some target.
explanation.walkthrough: PETA is People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, known for anti-pelt campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal pelts used in clothing are a chief campaign target for the animal-rights charity.

clue.text: Be angry about curtailed attempt to get garden tool

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes around the next letters

parts.note: to simmer is to be quietly angry

indicators.note: curtailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A gardener seethes over a short-lived attempt to get a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a powered grass trimmer used to cut lawn edges, a UK trademark.

clue.text: Yorkshire river, river that's different

parts.note: other means different

explanation.surface: Comparing a Yorkshire river with another that's not the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rother flows through South Yorkshire, joining the Don at Rotherham.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterway is a tributary of the Don in South Yorkshire, an example of the definition.
